messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: This lack of effect on other receptors is part of why Sertraline is described as selective.
How long does sertraline take to work?
:
Sertraline levels in the blood become steady after about a week of once daily dosing.
The effect on symptoms takes longer.
The trials that established sertraline ran for 6 to 12 weeks.
These trials were for depression.
These trials were for OCD.
These trials were for panic disorder.
These trials were for PTSD.
These trials were for social anxiety disorder.
The trials ran for over three menstrual cycles.
These trials were for PMDD.
This duration gives a sense of the time frame over which the benefit was measured.
It takes time.
Doses are usually raised no more often than once a week.
You should keep taking sertraline even if you do not feel a change yet.
How long does sertraline stay in your system?
:
Sertraline has a half-life of about 26 hours.
This means half of what is in your blood is cleared in roughly a day.
At that rate, most of a dose has left your bloodstream within about 5 to 6 days.
Triples: [["Sertraline", "has characteristic", "lack of effect on other receptors"], ["Sertraline", "has administration instruction", "take even if no change felt yet"], ["Sertraline", "has dosage adjustment instruction", "doses raised no more often than once a week"], ["Sertraline", "has blood level steady time", "about a week of once daily dosing"], ["Sertraline", "has effect onset time", "longer than blood levels steady"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "depression"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "OCD"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "panic disorder"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "PTSD"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "social anxiety disorder"], ["Sertraline", "used in clinical trials for", "PMDD"], ["Sertraline", "has trial duration", "6 to 12 weeks"], ["Sertraline", "has trial duration", "over three menstrual cycles"], ["Sertraline", "has benefit time frame", "6 to 12 weeks"], ["Sertraline", "has half life", "about 26 hours"], ["Sertraline", "has elimination time", "about 5 to 6 days"]]
Relations: ["has administration instruction", "has benefit time frame", "has blood level steady time", "has characteristic", "has dosage adjustment instruction", "has effect onset time", "has elimination time", "has half life", "has trial duration", "used in clinical trials for"]
Answer:

completion:
has administration instruction: The subject drug should be taken according to the specific instruction provided by the object entity.  
has benefit time frame: The therapeutic benefit of the subject drug is measured over the time frame specified by the object entity.  
has blood level steady time: The subject drug reaches a steady concentration in the blood after the time period specified by the object entity.  
has characteristic: The subject drug possesses the characteristic or property described by the object entity.  
has dosage adjustment instruction: The subject drug's dosage should be adjusted according to the specific instruction provided by the object entity.  
has effect onset time: The therapeutic effect of the subject drug begins after the time period specified by the object entity.  
has elimination time: The subject drug is largely eliminated from the body within the time period specified by the object entity.  
has half life: The subject drug has a half-life, which is the time it takes for half of the drug to be cleared from the body, as specified by the object entity.  
has trial duration: The clinical trials for the subject drug lasted for the duration specified by the object entity.  
used in clinical trials for: The subject drug was tested in clinical trials for the medical condition or disorder specified by the object entity.
